newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KNP BT still seeks Leykam partner.
newsitem.headline: KNP BT still seeks Leykam partner.

text.p: Dutch paper, printing and office machinery group NV Koninklijke KNP BT said on Thursday it was still looking for a partner for its paper division KNP Leykam but that it did not plan to sell off the unit.

"We expect further concentration in the paper market and we think that KNP Leykam is well positioned to participate in that process. We want to encourage them to try to find a partner which realises large synergies," KNP BT's financial director Rob Bonnier said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television.
He added that it was not KNP BT's intention to find a buyer for the whole of its 72 percent stake in KNP Leykam.
If a partner for the loss-making paper manufacturing division could be found, KNP BT would be prepared to dilute its stake in the unit, Bonnier said.
But he declined to say by how much KNP BT was prepared to reduce its stake, adding this depended on the future partner and what its contribution to an alliance would be.
"We still consider paper (production) as part of our core business," Bonnier said.
He said the signs on the paper markets were encouraging in terms of sales volumes and said KNP BT had more or less completely run down its paper inventories.
"The machines are running at full capacity," Bonnier said. But he warned that on the price side there was still a lot of uncertainty.
Selling prices were showing signs of an uptrend, but due to market uncertainty on the direction of raw material prices, players were hesitant to implement further price rises, he said.

KNP BT earlier reported third quarter net profit of 38 million guilders, down 67 percent from the year-ago period. KNP Leykam posted a seven million guilder operating loss, compared with a 108 million profit in the third quarter of 1995.
